feedback: Approve. The candidate is the iteration 5 design (score 403.4, best raced so far) with only the sensor row y moved from 0.05 m to 0.065 m. Sensor x positions, sensor_size 0.016, kp 2.6, kd 0.6, ki 0.1, base_speed 1.2, the sensor_weights, line_loss last_direction and the body, wheel and mass values are unchanged. The geometry is valid: y is within -0.06 to 0.08, and the rest is within range. The evidence for moving the row forward is the y trend. At y 0.03 (iteration 7, same controller) the score fell to 199.7, with oval finishes 4/20 against 17/20 at y 0.05 and s-bend finishes 0/20 against 1/20. Moving the row back from 0.05 cost about half the score, so the next step is to test more look-ahead, not less. Iteration 5 still had s-bend oscillation at 0.260 with 19/20 off-track endings and max_error 0.062, and that points to sensing lag. The lateral span of ±0.07 m is unchanged, so line loss should stay near the iteration 5 level (0.15 on the oval, 0.0 on the s-bend and slalom). The main risk is that extra look-ahead cuts corners on the tightest bends and raises max_error above 0.06. Racing this clean one-variable step gives more useful telemetry than another reading-only round, with three iterations left after this one. Next race, read the results as follows. If s-bend off-track endings fall, s-bend max_error stays under 0.06, line_loss_events stays near 0 and oval finishes hold at 17/20 or better, keep y 0.065 and raise base_speed in 0.1 steps (1.3, then 1.4) with kp and kd fixed, to test completion_time under 3 s. If s-bend max_error rises above 0.065 or oval finishes fall below 15/20, return y to 0.05 and test kd 0.5 at y 0.05 rather than moving the row again. If line_loss_events rises above about 0.3 on any track, return y to 0.05 before any other change.
